subject: History
topic: Vedic Age — Early and Later Vedic Period

questions.text: The Rig Veda, the oldest of the four Vedas, is primarily a collection of ____.

options.text: detailed sacrificial rituals and ceremony procedures
hymns (suktas) addressed to Vedic deities like Indra and Agni
philosophical dialogues on the nature of Brahman and Atman
astronomical calculations for fixing sacrificial calendars

questions.explanation: The Rig Veda (c. 1500–1200 BCE) contains 1,028 hymns (suktas) in praise of deities like Indra (war/rain), Agni (fire), and Varuna (cosmic order). Yajur Veda = sacrificial formulas; Sama Veda = melodic chants; Atharva Veda = charms and spells. The Rig Veda is the oldest human text of significant length.

questions.text: In the Early Vedic period (c. 1500–1000 BCE), the principal basis of wealth and economy was ____.

options.text: maritime trade with Mesopotamia and Southeast Asia
cattle herding in a semi-nomadic pastoral society
large-scale irrigated agriculture along canal networks
craft guilds producing metals and textiles for export

questions.explanation: Early Vedic society was predominantly pastoral. Cattle were the primary measure of wealth — the word for 'war' (gavisthi) literally means 'desire for cattle.' The Rig Veda repeatedly praises cows as the most valuable gift. Settled agriculture became dominant only in the Later Vedic period as the Aryans moved into the Gangetic plain.

questions.text: The Sabha and Samiti were two tribal assemblies in Vedic society. What was the key distinction between them?

options.text: Sabha was exclusively for women; Samiti was restricted to men only
Sabha was a smaller elite council of nobles; Samiti was a larger folk assembly
Sabha handled religious ceremonies; Samiti managed military campaigns
Sabha was a permanent judicial court; Samiti met only in wartime

questions.explanation: Sabha = select council of elders/nobles with advisory and quasi-judicial functions. Samiti = larger general assembly representing the whole tribe. Both are mentioned in the Rig Veda and served as checks on royal authority. These democratic-style assemblies gradually declined during the Later Vedic period as kingdoms grew more centralised.

questions.text: The Gayatri Mantra (Rig Veda 3.62.10), one of the most sacred Vedic hymns, is addressed to which deity?

options.text: Indra — chief deity, god of thunder and war
Savitri — the solar deity who illuminates the intellect
Agni — the fire deity, messenger between humans and gods
Varuna — guardian of cosmic order and moral law

questions.explanation: The Gayatri Mantra (RV 3.62.10) — 'Om Bhur Bhuva Swaha, Tat Saviturvarenyam...' — is a prayer to Savitri, the solar deity. It asks Savitri's divine light to illuminate and guide the worshipper's intellect. It is also called the Savitri Mantra. Indra is the most frequently praised deity in the Rig Veda overall, but the Gayatri is specifically addressed to Savitri.

questions.text: During the Later Vedic period (c. 1000–600 BCE), how did the varna system change compared to the Early Vedic period?

options.text: The number of varnas was formally reduced from four classes to just two main ones
Varna became birth-based and hereditary, replacing earlier occupational flexibility
The Kshatriya varna gained supreme religious authority over Brahmanas
The Shudra varna was formally elevated to equal the Vaishya status

questions.explanation: In the Rig Vedic period varna distinctions were relatively fluid (loosely occupational). By the Later Vedic period, varna became hereditary and birth-based, with Brahmins asserting supreme ritual authority. The Purusha Sukta (RV 10.90) — actually a later interpolation — provided cosmic justification for the four-varna hierarchy.

questions.text: The Painted Grey Ware (PGW) culture (c. 1100–600 BCE), found widely in the Gangetic Doab region, is archaeologically associated with ____.

options.text: the late urban phase of the Indus Valley Civilisation
the Later Vedic Aryans and the transition to Mahajanapadas
the administrative expansion of the Mauryan Empire
Megalithic Iron Age cultures of peninsular India

questions.explanation: PGW culture overlaps geographically and chronologically with the Later Vedic texts (Brahmanas, Aranyakas, Upanishads) and the Mahabharata setting (Hastinapura, Mathura, Kurukshetra). It marks a transitional phase from pastoral to settled agricultural society and the political consolidation into the 16 Mahajanapadas (~600 BCE).

questions.text: The Upanishads, composed during the Later Vedic period, are PRIMARILY concerned with ____.

options.text: detailed prescriptions for yajna rituals and their cosmic rewards
the relationship between Brahman (universal soul) and Atman (individual self)
astronomical calculations for accurate ritual calendar timings
graded social conduct rules for each of the four varna groups

questions.explanation: The Upanishads (also called Vedanta = 'end of the Vedas') shift focus from ritual (karma-kanda) to philosophical inquiry (jnana-kanda). Their core concern is the identity of Brahman (absolute universal reality) with Atman (the individual self). Core mahavakyas include 'Aham Brahmasmi' (I am Brahman) and 'Tat Tvam Asi' (That thou art). There are 108 Upanishads; 13 are principal.
